question.value: Constrain the physical conditions and mass-loss rate of an FUV-driven disk photoevaporation flow, and its implications for giant planet formation.

evidence.quote: Emission lines are detected from the PDR; modelling their kinematics and excitation allows us to constrain the physical conditions within the gas.
We quantify the mass-loss rate induced by the FUV irradiation, finding it is sufficient to remove gas from the disk in less than a million years.
ALMA observations were taken in December 2017 as part of project 2017.1.01478.S (Principal Investigator J. Champion).

referee_caveats_inferred: H2 geometry is inconsistent across sections: the main text uses radius 132 au and height 56 au; the methods use 132 and 59 au; Table S1 uses 127 and 56 au.
The H2 transition associated with the NIRCam geometry is labelled inconsistently, including 1→0, 1→2 and 2→1.
The NIRCam filter list contains F121N, whereas the emitting-layer analysis names F212N.
Dust UV absorption cross-section units are printed as cm−2; clarify these before constructing dynamical-model inputs.
Mass loss relies on an assumed flow speed near the sound speed rather than a directly measured expansion velocity.
The depletion estimate extrapolates the current mass-loss rate; time-dependent disk evolution is not demonstrated.
The 1D-model and observational mass-loss intervals overlap but do not agree over their full ranges.
